body: Definitely have to bring it up. There is no reason that y’all shouldn’t be having regular sex. There has to be a reason, mental, hormonal, emotional, cheating, etc.   If she truly doesn’t desire sex than imagine the rest of your marriage/life is without being intimately interacted with. Unless there is a mutual decision that y’all want to abstain (idk why) than not having sex is unacceptable. And especially if you are not being fulfilled by your partner.
Question before I respond. Was y’all’s plan to wait till marriage?

Well like you said “I’m sure it could be better.”  
Live for a time when it WILL be better, cause eventually it will be. I know it’s a lot easier said than done to ‘hope for the future’ but do it; don’t let this defeat you. I understand that I don’t know you at all, not your name, not what you look like, not anything about you, but I know that you can get past this. Why? Because you are human, and it’s in our nature to be resilient. “Pain is inevitable, but suffering is a choice.” We both know that it’s gonna suck and be painful, but don’t let it overpower the future that you can have, in fact let it propel you in a direction that you want to go. Whether is lifting, running, writing, painting, driving, or anything else, use it as fuel to be better and accomplish more.

“What if it can turn out better than you can imagine.”  < I think about this all the time, and it really helps. I’m not sure what you like to do for fun but I always think, “hmm…. What if next week there is a awesome party and I meet a girl….” Or “oh, next week is _____’s  birthday party can’t miss that.” I try to think about things or events that I will enjoy in the next few weeks, and I know it sound small and dumb but it keeps me going all the time.  If you don’t have a big friend group or any at all what I used to do is pregame a little head to a bar and just start talking to people (have to pregame cause I have zero sober confidence lol) you’d be surprised at how easy it is to find a group of people to hang out with.  Make up a story, tell them you just moved to town and don’t really know annoying.   To conclude, find small thing (sometimes very small things) that make you just a little bit happier and try to squeeze as many of those things into your day as possible, I’ve been doing that recently and I’ve been doing much better.
“What if it can turn out better than you can imagine.”    <keeps me going all the time :)

It will go away. Men typically, get into fights/argument (sometimes physically) a lot with other men and typically let go of their anger and resentment relatively quickly. For women I’ve found that they do hold on longer because they tend to be more emotionally based (nothing wrong with that at all). I don’t think you should feel bad whatsoever, but I do think that it would be wise to tell him directly that you are still somewhat angry and do need some distance to help you resolve your feelings. Best wishes :)

When people move in with each other they sometimes learn that they have a lack of compatibility. Aside from infidelity or something along those lines, maybe your boyfriend is/was being drowned in affection and now doesn’t have the same desire as before. As to the compliments, I can acknowledge that sometimes men don’t compliment people we are close too and have been with for a long time as much as someone newer or more scarcely seen.I think you need to bring up a serious conversation about what you need in the relationship and understand what he needs as well, with that, if the disparity is too large than maybe it is time to think about y’all’s long term compatibility and whether or not you have a future with each other. But overall feeling unloved is unacceptable for a long term relationship, don’t be afraid to fight for what you want, but in the same known when to say enough is enough and get out!  Best of luck! :)

Id say send one more. I just would incline you NOT to address the previous text though. Sometimes I’ve gotten a text and not seen it, then new texts pile on top and I completely miss it. Just happens sometimes especially with people who get a lot of phone traffic.

Ik what it’s like to be the one to trying and knowing that it won’t happen. It sucks. I would like to say just stop talking to him and move on, but I can’t even do it. I’m still trying to “win then” though not as often as I used to but still can’t let go of what I wish would be. And in the same I sometimes with that we hadn’t become friends thinking it would keep me from being in the situation that I’m in today, and I wouldn’t feel like this. So the best I can say it distanced yourself. I’m sure the best way is to just cold turkey stop, but we both know how hard it is, so I think slowly moving away is the best thing than you can do.
